authority_boundary: Technique cards are bounded candidate guidance. They do not authorize corpus access, provider egress, infrastructure, dependency adoption, production use, or changes to source truth.
coverage_statement: This is intentionally incomplete and versioned. It covers major current knowledge-engineering strategy families and requires local baselines, representative evaluation, counterevidence, and human gates rather than a universal stack.

techniques.label: No-retrieval direct source or deterministic navigation
query_shapes: known file or structured source navigation
applies_when: The authoritative source is already known and bounded.
A deterministic query or direct read meets the end goal.
does_not_apply_when: The corpus is too large or unknown to locate deterministically.
Cross-source ranking or semantic discovery is required.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Forcing RAG where direct source access is sufficient adds latency, cost, staleness, and false authority.
implementation_options: Existing source navigation or MCP resource
techniques.authority_boundary: The source system remains authoritative; the route cannot widen access or alter the source.

techniques.label: Direct long-context evidence assembly
applies_when: The relevant corpus fits the effective context budget.
Whole-document relationships matter more than selective retrieval.
does_not_apply_when: The corpus changes rapidly or exceeds cost/latency limits.
Access filters require selective evidence.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Advertised context length can conceal position, distraction, contradiction, latency, and cost failures.
implementation_options: Cached stable context with query-specific evidence
techniques.authority_boundary: A context window is a runtime capability claim, not authority or proof of effective recall.

techniques.label: Lexical and BM25 retrieval
applies_when: Exact token identity is informative.
A cheap explainable retrieval baseline is required.
does_not_apply_when: Queries and evidence use unrelated vocabulary.
Semantic paraphrase is the dominant signal.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Lexical-only retrieval can miss synonyms and conceptual matches while appearing precise.
techniques.authority_boundary: Rank is relevance evidence only and cannot override source authority or access controls.

techniques.label: Dense vector retrieval
applies_when: Semantic similarity adds recall beyond lexical search.
Embedding privacy and lifecycle are approved.
does_not_apply_when: Exact identifiers dominate.
Embedding/provider egress or retention is not approved.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Semantic similarity can blur authority, miss exact terms, leak sensitive meaning, and couple the system to an embedding identity.
privacy_security_requirements: Embeddings classified as derived sensitive data
Approved provider region retention and tenant isolation
techniques.authority_boundary: Embedding similarity is candidate relevance evidence, not semantic truth or identity.

techniques.label: Hybrid lexical+dense retrieval with rank fusion
applies_when: Lexical and dense lanes have complementary errors.
Fusion lift can be measured on representative queries.
does_not_apply_when: One cheaper lane already meets acceptance.
Scores or ranks cannot be reconciled reliably.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Uncalibrated fusion can amplify noisy lanes, obscure failure causes, and raise cost without recall lift.
techniques.authority_boundary: Fusion combines candidate ranks and cannot establish source truth.

techniques.label: Bounded second-stage reranking
applies_when: First-stage recall is adequate but ranking is weak.
Quality lift justifies added latency and cost.
does_not_apply_when: First-stage retrieval misses relevant evidence.
The candidate set or cost is unbounded.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: A reranker cannot recover absent evidence and may concentrate model bias or provider exposure.
techniques.authority_boundary: Reranking is candidate relevance evidence and cannot override filters, provenance, or source authority.

techniques.label: Source-faithful structural chunking
query_shapes: section paragraph table code legal and transcript retrieval
applies_when: Documents expose meaningful deterministic boundaries.
Citations must map back to exact source spans.
does_not_apply_when: Source extraction is too corrupt for reliable boundaries.
A whole bounded object is already the retrieval unit.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Boundary mistakes can detach context, tables, headings, or legal qualifiers while preserving a misleading citation.
prerequisites: Versioned parser and canonical source offsets
privacy_security_requirements: No source text copied across authority boundaries
techniques.authority_boundary: Chunks are derived projections and cannot redefine the canonical document.

techniques.label: Parent-child and neighborhood retrieval
applies_when: Small children improve matching but larger parents improve interpretation.
Parent identities and source spans are stable.
does_not_apply_when: Parents exceed context budgets.
Parent-child lineage is ambiguous or lossy.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Expanding to a broad parent can dilute relevance or expose unauthorized adjacent content.
evaluation_requirements: Child retrieval and parent answer lift
techniques.authority_boundary: Hierarchy is a derived navigation aid and cannot transfer source authority.

techniques.label: Contextual chunk enrichment before indexing
query_shapes: corpora where document context aids retrieval
applies_when: Failure analysis shows chunks lost document-specific context.
Generated context can be evaluated and retained separately.
does_not_apply_when: Structural metadata already supplies context.
Generation cost, privacy, or hallucination risk is unacceptable.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Generated context can invent facts, contaminate lexical indexes, and obscure the original source span.
privacy_security_requirements: Generated context never cited as source
techniques.authority_boundary: Context enrichment is generated metadata and cannot become source evidence.

techniques.label: Late chunking with long-context embeddings
applies_when: Long-context token embeddings are available and evaluated.
Local chunks lose surrounding semantic context.
does_not_apply_when: Documents exceed embedding context without a safe segmentation plan.
Embedding compute or migration cost is unacceptable.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Late chunking can appear source-faithful while coupling every chunk to a larger embedding context and expensive rebuilds.
prerequisites: Token-level embedding access or supported implementation
Stable chunk boundaries and document window
techniques.authority_boundary: Embedding context is a derived representation and cannot substitute for source spans.

techniques.label: Semantic or model-assisted chunk boundary selection
applies_when: Structural baselines fail on measured topic boundaries.
Boundary nondeterminism and cost can be governed.
does_not_apply_when: Authoritative structural boundaries exist.
Exact replay and citations cannot be preserved.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Model-selected boundaries may drift, merge unrelated authority, and become difficult to reproduce or cite.
privacy_security_requirements: No generated boundary changes source truth
techniques.authority_boundary: Semantic boundaries are experimental derived metadata until independently validated.

techniques.label: RAPTOR-style hierarchical summary retrieval
applies_when: Questions require both details and higher-level summaries.
Summary distortion can be evaluated against sources.
does_not_apply_when: Simple exact or local retrieval meets acceptance.
Generated summaries cannot be traced or refreshed reliably.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Recursive summaries can compound omissions or hallucinations and make stale derived claims look authoritative.
privacy_security_requirements: Generated summaries never replace canonical sources
techniques.authority_boundary: Hierarchical summaries are generated retrieval aids, not canonical claims.

techniques.label: Exact, HNSW, IVF, and vector-store selection
applies_when: Dense or multivector retrieval earned adoption.
Actual recall/latency/filter/operations requirements are known.
does_not_apply_when: Lexical or exact scan meets acceptance.
Canonical data, export, backup, or deletion cannot be preserved.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: A vendor or ANN choice can silently reduce filtered recall, isolate data poorly, or create costly lock-in.
evaluation_requirements: Recall/latency at concurrency and filter selectivity
Write freshness backup restore and export
operational_requirements: Capacity cost observability and disaster recovery
privacy_security_requirements: Region encryption retention and deletion review
techniques.authority_boundary: No engine is a universal winner; local workload and governance evidence control selection.

techniques.label: Authority-first metadata filtering and multitenancy
applies_when: Results must be constrained by authority before relevance.
Filter selectivity and recall can be tested.
does_not_apply_when: Metadata authority is missing or stale.
The engine cannot enforce the required isolation.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Post-filtering or inconsistent lane filters can leak data or return too few results while appearing successful.
techniques.authority_boundary: Relevance never widens authorization; unknown authority fails closed.

techniques.label: Graph-lite authoritative links and dependency projections
applies_when: Source systems already declare stable typed relationships.
Graph traversal improves routing or blast-radius analysis.
does_not_apply_when: Relationships would be inferred from similarity alone.
Source authority or edge semantics are unknown.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Generated or similar-looking edges can be mistaken for truth, approval, causality, or authority.
privacy_security_requirements: No sensitive labels or cross-boundary inference
techniques.authority_boundary: Graph presence, centrality, or traversal never proves truth, value, adoption, or authority.

techniques.label: GraphRAG entity, community, global, and local retrieval
applies_when: Hybrid text retrieval fails measured global or relationship questions.
Extraction and community costs are acceptable.
does_not_apply_when: Simple lookup or local retrieval meets acceptance.
Entity/link accuracy and prompt tuning cannot be evaluated.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Expensive extraction and generated communities can fabricate, merge, or stale relationships and summaries.
evaluation_requirements: Global/local answer lift and extraction cost
privacy_security_requirements: Generated claims retain source provenance and candidate status
techniques.authority_boundary: Graph extraction and community reports are candidate projections and cannot become source canon.

techniques.label: LightRAG-style graph+vector dual-level retrieval
applies_when: Graph and vector lanes have complementary evaluated value.
Incremental graph updates are a material requirement.
does_not_apply_when: Independent local evidence is absent.
Graph extraction or update consistency cannot be governed.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Paper-specific benchmark claims and lightweight naming can conceal extraction, consistency, and migration complexity.
privacy_security_requirements: No external model or store without approval
techniques.authority_boundary: Lightweight architecture or benchmark position does not authorize adoption or establish truth.

techniques.label: RDF, property, and provenance graph engineering
applies_when: Typed identifiers and cross-system semantics or graph traversal are durable requirements.
Standards/version compatibility is explicit.
does_not_apply_when: A table or document index is simpler and sufficient.
Ontology ownership or identity resolution is unknown.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Ontology and graph formalism can create false precision, duplicated authority, and expensive migrations.
techniques.authority_boundary: Standards describe representation and query semantics, not the truth or authority of populated claims.

techniques.label: Event, bitemporal, and temporal context graphs
applies_when: Valid time and observation/transaction time matter.
Superseded facts must remain traceable.
does_not_apply_when: Only current static facts are needed.
Time semantics or event provenance are absent.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: A current graph can be mistaken for history; invalidation or ingestion time can be confused with real-world validity.
privacy_security_requirements: Retention and deletion policy for history
techniques.authority_boundary: Generated temporal facts remain derived; canonical events and named source authorities control truth claims.

techniques.label: Agentic, self-reflective, and corrective retrieval
applies_when: Static routes have measured failure modes requiring adaptive recovery.
Tool scope, budgets, stops, and evidence are bounded.
does_not_apply_when: A deterministic route meets acceptance.
The agent could mutate corpora, indexes, ACLs, or external systems without exact authority.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Adaptive loops can increase nondeterminism, latency, cost, query drift, tool misuse, and evaluator self-confirmation.
prerequisites: Loop budget stop and fallback contract
evaluation_requirements: Cost latency tool and abstention behavior
techniques.authority_boundary: Adaptive selection does not grant mutation, access, promotion, or self-approval authority.

techniques.label: Multimodal and multivector retrieval
query_shapes: image table page and document retrieval
applies_when: Text extraction loses material visual evidence.
Multiple vector fields or token/region signals improve measured retrieval.
does_not_apply_when: Text/structure retrieval already meets acceptance.
Storage compute privacy or explainability costs are unbounded.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: High-dimensional or multivector indexes can inflate storage/cost and retrieve visually similar but evidentially irrelevant material.
operational_requirements: Fallback to text and source view
privacy_security_requirements: No OCR or vision output becomes source truth
techniques.authority_boundary: Multimodal similarity is candidate relevance evidence and must retain source localization.

techniques.label: Layered retrieval, answer, citation, graph, and operations evaluation
query_shapes: all production and high-consequence knowledge workflows
applies_when: Any retrieval, context, vector, graph, or agentic component is proposed.
A change or migration needs comparable evidence.
does_not_apply_when: No material knowledge-system decision exists.
Evidence cannot be separated from protected data safely.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: One aggregate or model-judge score can conceal missing retrieval, unsupported answers, access leaks, and operational failure.
prerequisites: Representative protected queries and source evidence
evaluation_requirements: Retrieval answer citation graph privacy robustness and operations gates
Independent human calibration for consequential slices
operational_requirements: Versioned gold set and contamination controls
privacy_security_requirements: No raw private traces in central telemetry
Evaluator cannot approve its own replacement
implementation_options: Human domain review and adversarial fixtures
techniques.authority_boundary: Evaluation is evidence for a named decision; it is not automatic promotion, deployment, or source authority.

techniques.label: Change capture, index lifecycle, migration, and retirement
query_shapes: embedding chunker database or graph migration
applies_when: Derived indexes must track source updates/deletes.
A component revision or provider change requires safe cutover.
does_not_apply_when: The corpus is a disposable immutable fixture.
Canonical sources or checkpoints are unavailable.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Silent in-place upgrades can mix incompatible embeddings, lose deletes, create split-brain results, and remove rollback.
evaluation_requirements: Shadow quality latency cost security and deletion parity
operational_requirements: Alias/router cutover bounded rollback and retirement receipt
privacy_security_requirements: Deletion across raw cache chunk vector graph and backup surfaces
techniques.authority_boundary: Lifecycle tooling cannot mutate live sources, indexes, routes, or schedules without exact authority.

techniques.label: Retrieval injection, poisoning, disclosure, and tenant-isolation controls
applies_when: Any external, user, generated, or cross-tenant content enters a knowledge system.
Retrieved material influences actions or claims.
does_not_apply_when: Only a fully synthetic isolated fixture is used and no reusable path exists.
techniques.danger_if_misapplied: Treating retrieved text as trusted instructions or failing tenant/provenance controls can leak data, poison answers, and cause tool misuse.
operational_requirements: Quarantine incident and verified deletion workflows
privacy_security_requirements: Retrieved content is untrusted data and tool authority stays separate
techniques.authority_boundary: Security controls can block unsafe routes but cannot authorize new corpus access or automated remediation.
